newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Euro shares ignore Greenspan but UK cautious.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Euro shares ignore Greenspan but UK cautious.

text.p: Continental European stock markets ignored warnings from U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan on Thursday, powering ahead after only the briefest of pauses for breath.
The German bourse rose close to its intraday record on the blue chip DAX index by late morning, while the Paris market was also up over one percent as investors largely reacted to domestic factors.
But London was more cautious, awaiting Wall Street's opening as dealers warned that European markets could not completely ignore any Greenspan hint on U.S. interest rates.
The dollar recouped some of its overnight losses against the yen and was stable against the mark.
Greenspan, who sent stock markets plunging for a while across the globe late last year when he warned investors against irrational exuberance, proved less influential this time.
On Wednesday he warned of excessive optimism over the U.S. economy, telling a Senate committee that caution was especially warranted due to the sharp rise in U.S. equity prices in the last two years.
He also hinted at the possible need to pre-empt inflation, implying higher interest rates.
His remarks gave Wall Street a bumpy ride, with the Dow Jones Industrial average closing down 55 points at 6,983.
But European investors were already losing interest by Wednesday's close after brief dips and the leading continental markets ignored Greenspan completely on Thursday.
French and German shares led the way at late morning, with the DAX up 1.4 percent at 3,283.82, just three points shy of the all-time high.
In Paris, the CAC-40 rose 1.05 percent or 27.40 points to 2,629.57, just five points below its closing high hit earlier this month.
French investors were more interested in good data on the troubled domestic economy than Greenspan.
GDP rose 0.2 percent in the fourth quarter of 1996 after a revised 0.8 percent rise in the third quarter, giving full-year growth of 1.3 percent.
"After Greenspan's statements and the drop on Wall Street, we were bracing for a decline today. But the GDP is a positive surprise," a Paris broker said.
London staged a less spectacular performance, with the FTSE up just 6.5 points at 4,335.8.
Activity was relatively subdued before the Wall Street open although attention was mostly on domestic corporate results and political events.

"We are looking a bit cautious ahead of Wall Street's performance today," said one senior trader. "We haven't taken too much notice of Mr Greenspan ourselves, but it doesn't mean we will ignore any change in the interest rate environment there."
A British parliamentary by-election on Thursday, in which the ruling Conservatives are expected to lose to the opposition Labour Party, is unlikely to depress stocks.
Some traditionally pro-Conservative investors would actually prefer a clear-cut Labour win to reduce the chance of no party winning decisively in the general election which has to be held by May.
"A Labour (by-election) victory is already priced in," said a trader. "A Conservative win would raise fears of a hung parliament at the general election and would impact on markets."
On the foreign exchnage markets, the dollar remained under pressure from a strong yen, although it was steady against the mark.

The dollar struggled to make headway against the yen after falling in early trade as investors continued to speculate about repatriation of funds by Japanese corporations before the end of their fiscal year in March.
"That's tending to drag the dollar down," said Glenn Davies, chief economist at Credit Lyonnais Laing here. "But it seems to us as though the dollar should be strengthening against the mark."
The dollar recovered a little from an early low of 120.36 yen to reach 121.08, albeit well below its late Wednesday European level of 122.15.
It was also at 1.6895 marks, unchanged from its level in late European trading on Wednesday.

Analysts expected the dollar to stabilise after its overnight fall against the yen. "This is a natural pause after a strong rise in recent weeks," said one. "The data are going to reaffirm the underlying strength of the dollar."
CURRENCIES AT 1130 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.6895 marks and 121.08 yen, compared with 1.6895 and 122.15 in late European trade on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1130 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 6.5 points at 4,335.8
PARIS - The CAC-40 was 27.40 points higher at 2,629.57.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index rose 45.95 points to 3,283.82.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was at $356.90 an ounce after being fixed in the morning at $356.60 and compared with $353.85 at the London close on Wednesday. Silver was three cents higher at $5.26.
